scope: RB2c logo set only; site, videos, launch kit not yet reviewed

first_glance.tab_16px: A small red pin or funnel stuck into a short black-and-grey comb; it reads as a marker on a ruler only once I already know the brief.
first_glance.readme_header: A red funnel on a stem standing on a row of piano-key bars, black on the left and grey on the right, beside a heavy wordmark.
first_glance.avatar_96: A red funnel or golf tee planted in a row of thick black and grey bars, like a keyboard or bar chart with a pin in it.
first_glance.avatar_20: A red blob on a stalk over a tiny black and grey stripe; reads as a red pin, with no ruler detail.
first_glance.mark_alone: A red funnel on a thin stalk standing in a keyboard-like row of chunky bars; the playhead idea is there second, the funnel and piano keys come first.

rows.item: Concept reads (playhead on a step ruler, scrubbed back)
rows.evidence: The two-tone split is the strongest idea and it works: black ticks left of the line are the recorded past, grey ticks right are the steps undone, and the red line sits on the cut. The shape language still fights the brief. The head is a flat-topped pentagon, but its sides taper into a long neck, so in the 1024 lockups (head about x478-614, y270-390) the whole thing still reads as a funnel or tee, which is the round 5 complaint only partly fixed. The ticks are now thick bars (about 30 px wide on a 1024 canvas) with narrow gaps, joined by a baseline, so the ruler reads as piano keys or a bar chart rather than a step ruler with hairline ticks. Neither the head nor the ticks look like a timeline tool at a glance.

In the real 16 px tab on the light and dark pages and in favicon-32.png, the red head, the line and a split black/grey tick row all survive with the rule at 1 px, and the dark version keeps the coral clearly separate from the ground. Silhouette is distinct and not mush. The nearest-neighbour 64 px tile is a true 4x of the 16 px drawing and shows a sensible pixel-built head. Drag: the head is only 5 px wide at the top, so at true size it is a red dot on a stem, and the tick row is about 4 ticks of equal weight, so it reads as a comb. At 20 px avatar crop, the ruler detail is mostly gone.

Bricolage Grotesque 800, lowercase, tight and even; r-e-w-i-n-d-a-g-e-n-t spacing has no gaps or collisions at 1024 (wordmark x136-890). The stacked lockup width ratio of mark to word is about 72 percent as specified, and in the horizontal lockup on the in-use sheet the rule bottom and playhead bottom sit on the text baseline. The wordmark is heavier than the mark in the horizontal lockup, which makes the small mark feel a size too small next to it, a minor point.

rows.item: Palette fidelity and distinctness from John's other brands
rows.evidence: Ground, ink, red on light, coral on dark and the grey tick colour match BRAND.md by eye and by the measured samples. The warm red and coral on near-black and off-white paper stand apart from John's other brands: no purple, no navy, no emblem or lock shape anywhere. The grey of the undone ticks is slightly low in contrast on the light ground but is deliberate and still legible.

logo-light and logo-dark are well balanced: mark and word centred on the 1024 square with generous margin, same layout on both grounds, and the dark version swaps to coral and light ticks cleanly. avatar-512 centres the mark (extent about x72-440, y152-360) with good air, and the whole thing holds inside the circle crops at 96, 48 and 20 px. Weaknesses: the avatar has no wordmark, so everything rides on the funnel-and-keys shape, which is the least resolved element; and the head is larger than the ruler is tall, so the top feels heavy.

1280x640: left-aligned stack of wordmark, tagline over two lines, the real command in a hairline box in Commit Mono, and credit line; the mark on the right is now vertically centred on the headline-to-command block (mark about y148-400, block about y105-445) and is larger, so the right half no longer feels empty. Hierarchy is clear and nothing is centred by default. Still weak: the mark is the unresolved funnel-on-keys at large size, where its faults are most visible, and the gap between command box and credit line is large and a bit loose.

No gradient, glow, shadow, emoji, 3D or mascot anywhere in the set. Flat fills only. The text content is limited to the wordmark, the tagline 'Ctrl+Z for AI coding agents: record, replay, rewind.', the command 'rewindagent rewind 12' (the stated real syntax, verified by a CLI-parsing test), the credit 'made by John B Joseph' and, on the in-use sheet, an install line with a repository path. No invented claims, no filler strings left on the in-use sheet. The install line should be checked by the same kind of test as the rewind command, since it is also presented as a real command.

fixes: Fix the head so it cannot read as a funnel: make it a short, wide flat-topped pentagon whose point sits directly on the rule with no visible neck, and make the line itself a hairline, so the head (about 3x the line width, shallow depth) is clearly a handle on a thin cursor line, not a cone on a stalk. Redo the 16 px pixel drawing to match.

Make the ruler read as a ruler, not a keyboard: thin the ticks to about a third of their present width with wider gaps, and add a taller major tick every fourth step (or vary heights) so it looks like a step scale with a hierarchy. Keep the black-past and grey-undone split, which works.

Rebalance the proportions after fixes 1 and 2: head height no more than about 40 percent of the tick row's visual weight, and in the horizontal lockup raise the mark a little in size relative to the heavy wordmark.

Re-render everything from the revised geometry (logos, avatar, favicon-32, social preview, 16 and 64 px tiles, in-use sheet) and re-check the first-glance reading at 96 and 16 px; the target reading is a playhead on a ruler in half a second.
Check the install line shown on the in-use sheet with the same parse-it-with-the-tool test as the rewind command, or remove it.
